versions.title: Nookly on your phone
versions.summary: The same Nookly on iPhone and iPad, always in step with your computer.

highlights.title: Nookly for iPhone and iPad
highlights.description: Sign in with your account and your whole Nookly is on your phone.

highlights.title: Live across devices
highlights.description: Edits show up on your other devices as you make them, and offline changes catch up when you reconnect.

highlights.title: You decide on clashes
highlights.description: When two devices changed the same thing, you pick a version or keep both. Nothing is lost.

Improved: Review Changes puts both versions side by side with line numbers, the other version in red and the one showing now in green, and marks the words that differ inside each line.
Fixed: In Vim's normal and visual mode the cursor is a block over the character it is on again.
When two devices changed the same thing at the same moment, the sync status and Settings now say a change needs a look.

highlights.title: Pictures travel with your exports
highlights.description: Exporting a note, jot, task or assignment as a Nookly file now includes its images, videos, sounds and files, so they appear when you import it elsewhere.

Improved: Nookly files can now be up to 100 MB to import.
Saving a Nookly file tells you if a file could not be included because it is missing.

highlights.title: Write a description right away
highlights.description: The quick New task and New assignment windows have a description below the title, with every block a page has, so you can write it before you create.

Improved: Agents using the Nookly command line can now read your Moodle courses, files, assignments, grades and announcements. They only read, and use the Moodle sign in you saved in Nookly.
The sidebar now slides in and out faster and more smoothly, including when it appears as you move the pointer to the left edge.

Fixed: Opening and closing Settings no longer makes the app freeze for a moment.
Opening the saved views under Tasks or Assignments in the sidebar no longer makes the move handle and arrow of that item jump down.
Dragging on the preview of a math block, equation, diagram, circuit or plot no longer picks up the whole block or drags its text. Mind map blocks still let you drag their ideas.

Improved: The import dialog for Moodle files is calmer and easier to use with a keyboard or screen reader, with searchable lists for labels and courses instead of a wall of chips.

Fixed: Fixed the Quick assignment and Settings shortcuts doing nothing until the dialog had been opened another way first.

Improved: Search and Quick open now show the ID of every result, like NOT-94, next to its title.

Fixed: Opening and closing the New task dialog, and other dialogs, is no longer slow on a long list of tasks or assignments.

Improved: You can now attach a file by its path from the sidebar of any page, and it shows whether Nookly can find it.

highlights.title: Files that tell you where they stand
highlights.description: A file you added by path now shows whether Nookly can find it. If it moved, or lives on another device, Locate points Nookly at it again here.

Improved: The actions on a file's page are grouped into opening it, where it lives, and changing it, and a file that only exists as a link now offers Copy into Nookly.

highlights.title: Add to a group of related items
highlights.description: Each group in the sidebar has its own plus button that opens the list of that kind of item, with a way to create a new one and link it right away.

Improved: The Relate to button is now called Link, and each step of the picker says what it asks.
You can now zoom the relationship graph out and in, or fit it to your view, so the second ring is fully visible.
Fixed: The relationship graph now scrolls up, down, left and right in one swipe when the second ring is on.

highlights.title: Mind maps
highlights.description: Write your ideas as an indented list and Nookly draws them as a map. Drag ideas where you want them, and click one to fold or open its branches.

Improved: The Calendar page in Settings shows a small week that follows your choices, with the settings grouped by what they change.
Fixed: The colour and intensity choices for the current day now work properly with screen readers.

Improved: On Mac, Nookly now tidies the list of apps allowed to read your saved logins, so it no longer collects an entry for every old version.

highlights.title: Pictures on flashcards
highlights.description: Cards are written in the note editor, so they can hold pictures, formulas, tables and more. Click a picture while studying to see it larger.

Improved: Shared deck files now include the pictures of their cards, and can be up to 100 MB.

Fixed: Calendar entries no longer show up in search, since they have no page of their own.

Nookly for Mac is now code signed, so updating no longer asks for your computer password again to reach your saved logins. This is not Apple notarization, so macOS may still show a warning the first time you open Nookly.
Links now always open in your default browser, never inside Nookly.

highlights.title: Drop files in
highlights.description: Drop files onto the Files page to import them, onto a page to attach them, or into a note to place them where the drop area shows.

Fixed: Fixed dragging a file onto Nookly covering the whole app with that file until you restarted.

Improved: Moving an item to Trash no longer asks first. It happens right away, and a message with Undo appears so you can bring it back at once.
C is now a language you can pick for code blocks.
A file now fills its page without a margin or border around it, the same as a file from Moodle.

Fixed: Fixed opening a note sometimes showing "Something went wrong showing this view" until you pressed Try Again.

highlights.title: See how things connect
highlights.description: The new graph button next to Pin shows an item with everything it links to around it. Turn on Second ring to look one step further, and click to open.

highlights.title: Smarter Moodle imports
highlights.description: Importing a Moodle file now lets you rename it, pick labels and attach it to a course first, with suggestions ready.

highlights.title: Show in Nookly
highlights.description: Moodle files you already imported show a button that takes you straight to them.

highlights.title: Choose your page font and size
highlights.description: Pick a default, serif or mono font and a text size for your pages under Settings, Editor, and see a live sample as you change them.

Fixed: The closed unexpectedly message no longer shows up after an update, and its buttons now fit inside the window.

highlights.title: Moodle inside Nookly
highlights.description: Read your courses, open and import files, check assignments and grades and read announcements. Add the Moodle module to a Space to connect.

highlights.title: Moodle deadlines on your calendar
highlights.description: Connect the link from Moodle's Export calendar under Calendar connections to see deadlines next to your sessions.

highlights.title: Copy a file's text
highlights.description: Text, code and Markdown files have a copy button at the top right of the viewer.

versions.title: A faster, simpler search
versions.summary: Search shows one list of results, best match first, and you can narrow it by typing.

highlights.title: One list of results
highlights.description: Every result shows its icon, title, Space and the line that matched. The best match is already selected, so Enter opens it.

highlights.title: Filter by typing
highlights.description: Type in: to pick a Space or # to pick a label, and press Tab to switch between types like Notes, Tasks and Files.

highlights.title: Open results where you want
highlights.description: Open the selected result in a new tab, or in the other side of a split.

Improved: Quick open now looks at titles only, so it answers instantly.
Search opens right away and starts looking on your first keystroke.

versions.title: A tidier Settings
versions.summary: Settings is easier to scan, and the pages look like what they hold.

highlights.title: A flat list of pages
highlights.description: Every page is in one list under short headings, and search sits at the top. Press the slash key to jump to it.

highlights.title: Pick a theme by sight
highlights.description: Light, dark and system are cards with a small preview, and the file viewer theme works the same way.

highlights.title: Shortcuts in a table
highlights.description: All your shortcuts are on one page. Use the buttons at the top to show only one group, like Tabs or Create.

Improved: The Backup page shows when the last backup was made, how big it is and where it is saved, and says clearly if one failed.
Google Calendar and iCloud have their own Connections page in Settings, with a card that shows whether each one is connected.
LaTeX macros have their own page under Power tools in Settings.
A shortcut whose key was taken by another one is marked in the list.
Fixed: On Mac, your Nookly data folder now opens in Finder with a double click. It is called Nookly, and nothing is moved or copied.

highlights.title: Report after an unexpected close
highlights.description: If Nookly closes unexpectedly, you can read, copy or share a short report next time. It never holds what you wrote, and nothing is sent unless you send it.

highlights.title: Logs for bug reports
highlights.description: Nookly keeps a short log of problems, never what you wrote. Open the folder from Settings and attach it when you report a bug.

Improved: Nookly starts quicker and takes less space.
Lists and searches no longer hold up the rest of the window, and Nookly no longer reloads everything each time you switch back to it.
Fixed: When something goes wrong behind the scenes, Nookly now shows an error instead of closing.
Dragging tabs to reorder or split them, and dragging semesters to reorder them, now works on Linux.
The icon and name of each module in the sidebar no longer cover the handle you drag to reorder them.

versions.title: A calmer sidebar
versions.summary: The sidebar now shows one Space at a time, with all your Spaces in a row at the bottom.

highlights.title: One Space at a time
highlights.description: See only the modules of the Space you are in, and switch from the row of Spaces at the bottom. Right click a Space to rename it or change its icon or color.

highlights.title: Switch Spaces quickly
highlights.description: Swipe sideways with two fingers and the list moves with your fingers, springing back if you let go early. Or step through your Spaces with the keyboard.

Improved: The plus at the bottom left of the sidebar adds a new Space or a module to your current Space.
Trash and Collapse sidebar are now small icons next to your Spaces.
A short hint at the bottom of the sidebar tells you about swiping between Spaces, and goes away once you have tried it.

Fixed: Typing `^` in an empty code or math block no longer breaks the block.

highlights.title: Fit Width for PDFs
highlights.description: A new button in the PDF toolbar makes the page as wide as the viewer.

Improved: Zooming a PDF changes the size by the same share at every level, and pinching zooms around your cursor.
Zooming and scrolling through long PDFs is faster.
Fixed: Pages no longer jump around while a PDF with pages of different sizes loads.
Very large pages at a high zoom no longer turn blank.

Improved: A new assignment from the quick assignment shortcut opens in a background tab, so you stay in your jot or note.

highlights.title: Vectors in plots
highlights.description: Draw an arrow between two points with `(0, 0) -> A` or `A -> B`. Name vectors with `a = 0 -> A`, then draw `a + b` and `a - b`.

Improved: The legend of a plot shows each line as a formula, with fractions, roots and subscripts.
Start a line in a plot with `!#` to use it without showing it, for example a point that only a vector needs.
A line like `z_1 = 2` is drawn as a horizontal line, without needing `(x)`.

versions.title: Spell checker, links that open Nookly and more
versions.summary: Check your spelling, link to files and selected text, and get a lot more done from the keyboard.

highlights.title: Share a file
highlights.description: Send a file to someone from its details sidebar, with the share button at the top or **Share** in the more actions menu.

highlights.title: Assembly code blocks
highlights.description: Pick **Assembly** as the language of a code block to see instructions, registers, labels and numbers in their own colors.

highlights.title: AI Comment callout
highlights.description: Mark what an AI changed with the new purple **AI Comment** callout, so it stands out from your own notes and the standard callouts.

highlights.title: Duplicate a line
highlights.description: Press the shortcut in a page to copy the line you are on right below it, for text, list entries, tasks and code.

highlights.title: Refine side by side
highlights.description: Refine a jot into a note and both open next to each other, so you can read the jot while you write the note.

highlights.title: Readable mentions
highlights.description: A mention you copy or export now names the page by its short ID, like **JOT-12**, instead of a long code. Older mentions keep working.

highlights.title: Find a heading by typing
highlights.description: On a long page, open the section list at the bottom and type to find a heading. The match is marked, and **Enter** jumps to it.

highlights.title: Quick assignment
highlights.description: Create an assignment from anywhere. During a session it starts in that session's course and links to the session.

highlights.title: Table row and column menus
highlights.description: Right click the grip next to a table row or above a column to add, duplicate, move, clear or delete it, or to copy a mention that points at it.

highlights.title: Open in an AI app
highlights.description: On the Agent tab in Settings, **Open in** shows the AI apps on your computer and opens your agent folder in the one you pick.

highlights.title: Files by path
highlights.description: The **/file** block now takes the full path of a file on your computer. If the file is not there, the block says why and keeps the path until it is back.

highlights.title: Links that open Nookly
highlights.description: Right click an item or a block and choose **Copy Link**. Clicking that link anywhere on your computer opens Nookly on it.

highlights.title: Spell checker
highlights.description: Misspelled words get a wavy underline and a right click offers corrections. Pick several languages, like **English and German**. Off until you turn it on.

highlights.title: Link to selected text
highlights.description: Select text, right click and choose **Copy Mention for Selection** or **Copy Link for Selection**. Opening it selects that text on the page.

Improved: Copying a mention is now called Copy Mention, and Copy Link now copies a link that opens Nookly.
Related items in the details sidebar are grouped in a fixed order, starting with bookmarks, assignments, tasks and notes.
Settings has a page for each group of shortcuts, and lists the keys of the page editor, like bold, headings and lists.
Pages under a category in Settings, like LaTeX, hang on a guide line under it instead of showing an arrow icon.
The words you add to the spell checker are kept in a plain file, dictionary.json, which Show dictionary file in Settings shows in Finder.
When an assignment is due before a specific session, you pick it from a week of your calendar, so you can see which session is which.
The due date menu always opens below the field.
Fixed: An assignment due before the next session now stays on that session once it starts, instead of moving on to the one after it.

highlights.title: Plots
highlights.description: Type **/plot** and write `f(x) = x^2 - 2` or `A = (1, 2)`, one per line, to see them in a coordinate system. Set the view with `window: -10..10`.

highlights.title: New task from anywhere
highlights.description: Open the New task dialog wherever you are and start typing the title right away. **New Task** in the command menu opens it too.

Fixed: Inline math in PDF, Word and OpenDocument exports shows as real formulas instead of raw LaTeX, and Word files get equations you can edit.

highlights.title: Colored text
highlights.description: Select text in a Note or Jot and pick a color from the bar below it.

Improved: A file in a page can name the last page of its interval, like pages 3 to 9.
Exports to PDF, Word and OpenDocument start on A4 instead of Letter.
Cmd or Ctrl and a click on a file in a page opens it in a new Nookly tab.
The Open settings file button is now called Show settings file.

highlights.title: Export as PDF, Word or OpenDocument
highlights.description: Choose **Export...** on a Note or Jot to save it as a PDF, Word or OpenDocument file, with a preview of every page and the title on top if you like.

Improved: Saving a page as Markdown now happens in the same Export dialog.

highlights.title: Filter with OR
highlights.description: Show items that match either filter. Click **and** between two filters to switch it to **or**.

Improved: Clear filters always sits next to the Filter button, above your filters.
Assignments can be filtered by when they were evaluated.
The Completed filter for Tasks is now called Completed at.
Every Filter menu lists its filters alphabetically.

Fixed: Files scroll smoothly even with hundreds of PDFs, without lag or blank gaps.

Improved: The title, search and filters of Notes and Jots stay in view while the list scrolls underneath.
Fixed: Notes and Jots open quicker and keep up while you type, even with thousands of entries.
Quick filters now star a filter such as Course in the Filter menu, and one click opens its choices.
Titles and buttons at the top of a page, such as the Calendar's, move onto a second line instead of overlapping in split view.

highlights.title: A fuller course page
highlights.description: See this week's sessions, plus the course's assignments, recent notes and exams, all on one page.

Improved: The next session tile on a course page names the session as well as its day and time.

highlights.title: Find in page
highlights.description: Search a page, step through each match and replace one or all. Match case, whole words or patterns, and put a cursor in every match at once.

highlights.title: Zoom a group
highlights.description: Hide the other side of a split view until you press the shortcut again, or pick **Zoom Group** in a tab's menu.

Fixed: Fixed the spacing around the tabs in split view.

Improved: Notes and Jots grow wider in a large window, so the empty sides next to the text get smaller.

Fixed: A formula no longer comes back as plain text with its dollar signs after a reload when it ended in a space, ran over two lines, held a dollar sign or had a digit right after it.
The LaTeX page in Settings stays indented and shows a corner icon to mark it as part of Editor.
Decks on the dashboard are no longer squeezed: a narrow card stacks its name, counts and Study button.

Improved: Tabs show the ID of their page, such as TSK-14, so similar names are easy to tell apart.
On a file or bookmark, **Relate to** now offers *Attached to*, so you can attach it to a page from its own side.

Fixed: Quick open, commands, search and every list in a menu find "Übungsblatt" whether you type "Übungs" or "ubungs".

highlights.title: Upload File
highlights.description: The attach menu in the details sidebar has an **Upload File** button at the top that adds a file to Nookly and attaches it to the page at once.

Fixed: Long label names no longer squash their checkbox in the label picker.
Markdown files with a `---` divider or front matter no longer open empty.
Markdown files open dark by default, like code and text files.
Markdown files no longer have extra space on the left.

versions.title: Ungraded homework, formulas in decks and a smarter slash menu
versions.summary: Mark assignments as ungraded, write display formulas on deck cards and find blocks faster with the slash menu.

highlights.title: Ungraded assignments
highlights.description: Set an assignment's **Evaluation** to Ungraded for homework, or Graded to add a grade. Ungraded work stays out of the course grade.

highlights.title: Formulas in deck cards
highlights.description: Write `$$…$$` for a formula on its own line and see a preview while you type the card.

highlights.title: Smarter slash menu
highlights.description: Type `/h2`, `/title` or just a few letters in order, like `/bkmk`, to find a block.

Fixed: Dollar amounts such as $5 and $10 in a deck card stay text instead of turning into a formula.
Decks on the dashboard look better when space is tight.
Hiding or showing the details sidebar in split view only changes the side you are working in.
The dashboard summary mentions a session that is about to start only once.

Improved: Long pages render in full again: parts scrolled out of view are no longer skipped.
Split Right and Split Left use `Mod+Alt+Shift+Right` and `Mod+Alt+Shift+Left`, so they no longer clash with selecting text.

highlights.title: Split view
highlights.description: Use the **Split** button, the command palettes or the keyboard to work side by side. `Mod+1` and `Mod+2` switch sides.

Improved: Lists, grids and the details sidebar fit the width of their side of a split.
Long pages stay smooth: parts scrolled out of view are not laid out until you get there.
Fixed: Tabs are announced once by screen readers, without their close button.
The section list in the floating progress pill stops growing at a comfortable height and scrolls when a page has many headings.

versions.title: A big batch of improvements
versions.summary: Vim keys, highlights, pinned columns, your own LaTeX commands and many smaller fixes.

highlights.title: Vim keys in pages
highlights.description: An early version of Vim controls, for pages only. Turn on **Vim keys in pages** under Settings, Editor, and press `?` in normal mode for the keys.

highlights.title: Highlight text
highlights.description: Type `==text==` or select text and press `Mod+Shift+H` to mark it with a highlighter.

highlights.title: Your own LaTeX commands
highlights.description: Add your own commands under Settings, Editor, LaTeX, each with a live preview, starting with a few common ones, and use them in every formula.

highlights.title: Pin table columns
highlights.description: Use the pin button in the table toolbar to keep the first columns in place while a wide table scrolls sideways.

highlights.title: Format code blocks
highlights.description: Tidy a code block with the Format button in its header, or turn on **Format code when pasted** in Settings. Undo brings the old code back.

highlights.title: Open a file on a page
highlights.description: Set a page number on a file in a note and it opens on that page, so each note can point to its own part of the same PDF.

highlights.title: Make today stand out
highlights.description: Pick a colour and intensity for the current day in the calendar under Settings.

Improved: The command palette has a New Tab action, with its shortcut shown next to it.
Attachments in the detail sidebar are grouped by type, like Relationships.
Customize sidebar can now hide Trash too.
The sentence at the top of the Dashboard names only your next session.
Search lists results that start with what you typed first, so `/in` shows Inline math before headings.
Fixed: Deleting everything inside inline code, or a highlight, removes it, so the line is plain again. The right arrow steps out of it at its end, and the left arrow at the start of a line, with a small gap showing where the caret is.
Bullet points fixed: an indented item keeps its letter or number, and a numbered list can start anywhere, like `b)`, `c.` or `12.`, and carries on from there.
Tab nests a bullet under the one above it, nested items are saved with the page, and Tab no longer jumps out of the editor on the first bullet.
A zoomed PDF or document keeps its sideways scroll position when you switch tabs, as well as its place down the page.
Scrolling a wide table sideways no longer carries the table controls out of reach.
Inserting a Math block, Equation, Diagram or Circuit from the slash menu no longer swallows the text above it.
Cmd+Left on a line with inline math goes to the start of the line, not the top of the note.
Done tasks and assignments with a past due date read like "3 days ago" and never show as overdue.
The main content panel lines up with the left navigation panel at the top and bottom.

versions.title: Small things, done
versions.summary: Copy IDs, open embedded files and a handful of fixes.

Fixed: Typing after `@` in a page is fast again.
PDFs keep their zoom when you switch tabs, and spreadsheets come back on the same sheet.
Notes keep their scroll position when you switch tabs, and no longer jump to the bottom while loading.
The Dashboard calendar's date header, current time line and scrollbar no longer show over the corner cutout when scrolled.
Searching finds names with accents, so `Ü` or `ubung` finds a file called Übungsblatt in mentions, lists, the Trash and relationship suggestions.
Improved: Right click any item and choose Copy ID, right below Copy Link, to copy the ID you see on it, like `TSK-12`.
Click a file embedded in a page to open it in Nookly, or use Open in Nookly on its toolbar.
The Dashboard calendar keeps a minimum height of 800 pixels.
The Dashboard calendar opens two hours before now and keeps a comfortable height even when you have no Jots.

highlights.title: Your day at a glance
highlights.description: Assignments, Tasks, Decks, Jots and today's calendar sit side by side, each showing what matters most first.

Improved: Decks with cards to study today show a play button and leave once you are done.
Jots now list the oldest first.
The sentence at the top of the Dashboard greets you by name, leaves out sessions that already started and points out what matters most. Set your name in Settings under General.
Dashboard links and Show more open Tasks, Assignments or Jots with the matching filters already applied.
Assignments "For today" lists only those tied to a session today, including submitted and graded ones, for presenting in lectures.
Dashboard rows show their Space and a copyable ID, and due dates read as Today, Tomorrow or in 4 days.
Fixed: Tasks due today no longer go missing from the Dashboard sentence for a couple of hours after midnight.

Improved: Agent files appear in a list beside the text instead of tabs above it, and you can keep them in folders.

Fixed: The update card and What's new dialog now appear even when Nookly never noted which version you last saw.

Improved: The page has the same border as the left navigation, and it goes away when the sidebar is collapsed.
What's new lists every version since the one you were on, newest first, instead of only the latest.

versions.title: Tasks, decks and assignments travel too
versions.summary: Export a task, a deck or an assignment as a Nookly file and bring it back with Import, on this Nookly or another one.

highlights.title: Export a task
highlights.description: Save a task with its subtasks, status, dates and description from its **more actions** menu.

highlights.title: Export a deck
highlights.description: A deck leaves with its cards. Review history stays with you, so imported cards start as new.

highlights.title: Export an assignment
highlights.description: Keep its status, due day, grade and description. When you import it, you choose the course it belongs to.

highlights.title: Import any Nookly file
highlights.description: The Import dialog recognises pages, tasks, decks and assignments and shows what is inside before you confirm.

highlights.title: From the command line
highlights.description: `nookly cli task export` and `import` work for notes, jots, tasks, decks and assignments too.

Improved: Importing never changes what you already have. A bad file is refused with a clear reason and creates nothing.
Labels, links, the Space and review history are never part of a file.

versions.title: Bring pages in, share them out, and link things the easy way
versions.summary: Import and share pages, jot into the session that is running, and a calmer way to relate things to each other.

highlights.title: Import a page
highlights.description: Drop in a page exported from Nookly, choose the Space, relate it to what you have and check what it contains first.

highlights.title: Share a page
highlights.description: Send a page as Markdown or as a Nookly page file through the share menu of your system.

highlights.title: Jot for the session now
highlights.description: Open the jot of the session that is running **right now**, or get told there is none.

highlights.title: Relate in three steps
highlights.description: Pick the **type**, then **how**, then **which one**. Suggestions put the notes of the same course first.

highlights.title: Repeating tasks
highlights.description: Make a task repeat. Finishing it creates the next one.

highlights.title: Agent files
highlights.description: Keep instructions for your own coding agent in Settings, with a starter `AGENTS.md` and a guide to the CLI.

highlights.title: Symbols and emoji
highlights.description: Type `:` in a note and pick a symbol or an emoji, with the common ones ready.

highlights.title: Mention a page of a file
highlights.description: Press the right arrow on a file in the @ menu to pick a page. Clicking the mention opens the file there.

Improved: Search by day or time (Mar 10, Tuesday, 9am) when you relate to, mention or pick a session.
The @ menu groups notes, files, sessions and the rest under their own headings.
Renaming anything updates the mentions of it.
Notifications have a close button, a Clear all bar and their own icon for each kind. Errors stay until you close them.
Wide tables scroll sideways, and table columns can be dragged to a new place.
`Tab` and `Shift+Tab` indent text, and `Mod+Shift+V` pastes without formatting.
Click with **Cmd** (or **Ctrl**) held to open links, images and files.
Every tab remembers where you scrolled to.
Boards can hide a column, and the Assignments item shows the next one that is due.
The time field starts at the hour wherever you click it.
Fixed: A PDF that comes back after being unavailable no longer leaves Nookly blank.
The @ and / menus open again after you have closed them.
Long folder paths no longer run out of the Settings dialog.
